record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: How should the federated learning community define standard evaluation metrics and establish benchmark datasets that are appropriate for the major deployment settings, especially cross-device and cross-silo federated learning, so that proposed methods can be compared on realistic and broadly accepted criteria rather than ad hoc simulations?

evidence.quote: Developing standard evaluation metrics and establishing standard benchmark datasets for different federated learning settings (cross-device and cross-silo) remain highly important directions for ongoing work.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the federated learning setting in which a population of clients (data-holding parties) collaboratively trains a shared statistical model under the coordination of a central server, without exchanging raw local data. Two principal deployment regimes are distinguished:

(a) Cross-device federated learning: the client population consists of a very large number (potentially millions) of unreliable, resource-constrained devices (e.g., mobile phones), each holding a small, non-IID local dataset; only a small random subset participates in any round, and clients may drop out.

(b) Cross-silo federated learning: the client population consists of a small number (typically 2–100) of reliable organizational participants (e.g., hospitals, banks), each holding a large local dataset, with stable availability across rounds.

Design a principled framework for the empirical evaluation of federated learning algorithms by accomplishing the following:

1. Specify a set of standard quantitative evaluation metrics that jointly capture (i) model utility (e.g., predictive accuracy, calibration, fairness across clients), (ii) communication cost (uplink/downlink bytes per round and to convergence), (iii) on-device computation and memory cost, (iv) client participation efficiency (rounds-to-accuracy under realistic availability and dropout models), (v) robustness to heterogeneity in data distributions and system characteristics, (vi) privacy guarantees (e.g., differential-privacy budget (ε, δ)), and (vii) robustness to adversarial or Byzantine clients.

2. Construct standard benchmark datasets and accompanying client-partitioning schemes that faithfully reflect the statistical and systems heterogeneity of each regime, with explicit, reproducible protocols for client sampling, data non-IID-ness, availability patterns, and dropout, separately tailored to (a) and (b).

3. Provide a precise comparison protocol under which any two proposed federated learning methods can be ranked on the above metrics in a manner that is realistic, reproducible, and broadly accepted, replacing ad hoc simulation choices.

State criteria a proposed metric set and benchmark suite must satisfy to be deemed adequate for each regime, and exhibit such metrics, datasets, and a protocol meeting these criteria.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of establishing universally accepted benchmarks and evaluation metrics for federated learning remains an active and unresolved research direction. While benchmark suites such as LEAF, FedML, FLamby (cross-silo healthcare), FedScale, and pFL-Bench have been proposed since 2018, no single standard has been adopted by the community, and surveys through 2024–2025 continue to list standardized FL benchmarking as an open challenge, particularly for realistic cross-device system dynamics and for cross-silo regulated-domain settings.

status_evidence.title: LEAF: A Benchmark for Federated Settings
status_evidence.snippet: LEAF is a modular benchmarking framework with open-source datasets and reference implementations for federated learning.
status_evidence.claim: Early benchmark suite addressing FL evaluation, but not adopted as a single community standard.

status_evidence.title: FedScale: Benchmarking Model and System Performance of Federated Learning at Scale
status_evidence.snippet: FedScale provides realistic datasets and a runtime to evaluate FL algorithms with system heterogeneity at scale.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent benchmark addressing systems realism in cross-device FL; community standard still not settled.

status_evidence.title: FLamby: Datasets and Benchmarks for Cross-Silo Federated Learning in Realistic Healthcare Settings
status_evidence.snippet: FLamby is a benchmark suite focused on cross-silo healthcare FL with real-world datasets.
status_evidence.claim: Cross-silo benchmarking is being pursued but no universally accepted standard exists.

status_evidence.title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Standard evaluation metrics and benchmark datasets for cross-device and cross-silo FL remain important open directions.
status_evidence.claim: The need for standard FL metrics and benchmarks is identified as ongoing/open.
